claims.author: ajtowns
claims.quote: the lifetime of the budget there is just the wrapper, which seems fairly explicit to me?
claims.request: Consider the wrapper approach where the budget lifetime is explicitly scoped to the wrapper or ParamsStream rather than using mutable state on streams.

status_by.quote: I've switched to your approach, but added a feature for parameters to declare they cannot be overridden

claims.status_note: author adopted wrapper approach with non-overridable parameter feature

claims.author: maflcko
claims.quote: Are they really worth the complexity (and minimal cpu cost) when there are other places in Bitcoin Core that can eat memory (including in p2p). Are we going to address all of them?
claims.request: Explain whether the complexity and minimal CPU cost of the last few commits is worth it given other memory-eating places in Bitcoin Core.

status_by.quote: FWIW, the point is reducing the time to deserialize a pathological non-segwit 4 MB transactions (which would be 16 MWU)... I'll redo the benchmarks to justify it.

claims.status_note: author explained it targets pathological non-segwit 4MB txs and promised to redo benchmarks

claims.author: Yudis-bit
claims.harm: Oversized blocks failing deserialization are not disconnected, so the block request stays in mapBlocksInFlight until the 10-minute download timeout expires, potentially stalling block download.
claims.quote: Since the peer isn't disconnected, the hash stays in mapBlocksInFlight until the 10-minute download timeout expires.

status_by.quote: That's a fair concern. It's no different from how we treat a peer that never responds to a `getdata` requests at all

claims.status_note: author noted it's similar to peers not responding to getdata, and will investigate blanket disconnects separately
